items.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

ctx.x: We used to live in the Belmont place. And, uh, in New Orleans. And, uh, he started taking lessons on it, you know. Yeah. And then, uh, and, uh, actually my father bought me a banjo. And I started learning the banjo. I just left Oliver. I was with him, uh, I stayed in Chicago almost three weeks. He was with me most all the time. Yeah. Yeah. His mother, his mother's here now visiting. He got three, he got two sisters out here. Yeah. Yeah. And a brother, one brother. And, uh, I'm surprised he's not out here now.…

I can show you a picture of Oliver. That's him. Yeah. Yeah, that's Alvin. Do you know who gave me this picture? Mrs. Nolling. Miss who? Nolling. I don't know. Ransom Nolling, the bass player. I don't know. I got his address. Yeah, I got it too. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. 61 and something. That's right. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Those, those, why had to raise up with those boys. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Do you, do you know if he was related to George McCollum Jr.?
